title: Post-launch retro: cross-language SDK parity (auth/retry/timeouts/streaming)
creator: Talia Benson
description: Run a post-launch retro for the SDK parity initiative. Capture what worked/failed, metrics + customer feedback, any remaining parity gaps, and concrete follow-ups with owners/dates. Output should feed into: next parity iteration plan, support playbook, and release checklist improvements.
acceptance_criteria:
- Retro notes captured in this ticket (decisions, what went well, what didn’t)
- Remaining parity gaps listed with clear next steps (issue links or TODOs)
- Action items have owners + target dates
- Add 2–3 process changes to prevent repeat issues (CI/conformance/release checklist/docs)
- Share summary in #devex and link from ENG-5120 epic
content:
## Context
This ticket captures the post-launch retro for the cross-language SDK parity initiative (Python/TypeScript/Go) covering:
- auth resolution order + env vars
- retry/backoff defaults + Retry-After
- timeout model
- streaming semantics + disconnect handling
- error taxonomy + request_id propagation
- conformance test suite adoption

Launch window: beta → stable releases shipped over ~2 weeks, with platform gateway changes landing in parallel.

## Attendees
- Monica Patel (DRI)
- Ibrahim Khan (Tech lead)
- Dana Lo (TS)
- Mateusz Zielinski (Go)
- Sabrina James (Python)
- Allison Grant (SRE/standards)
- Marcus Lin (Security)
- Elliot Price / Wei Chen (Docs)
- Dev Patel / Owen Phillips (Support)
- Connor O’Brien (Release coord)
- Talia Benson (Program)

## Artifacts
- Parity matrix (current vs desired): sources/confluence/eng-developer-experience/sdk-guides/sdk-parity-matrix-auth-retry-timeouts-streaming.json
- Retry/timeout standard: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/sdk-retry-timeout-standard.json
- Auth + secret handling guidance: sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/sdk-auth-resolution-and-secret-handling.json
- Migration notes: sources/confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/sdk-migration-notes-auth-retry-timeout.json
- Streaming quickstart: sources/confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/streaming-quickstart-consistent-behavior.json
- SRE retry impact analysis: sources/confluence/eng-sre/reliability-initiatives/sdk-client-retry-impact-analysis.json

## What shipped (v1)
1) Auth
- Standardized resolution order across SDKs: explicit client param > env vars (new names) > legacy env vars (deprecated) > error
- Secret handling: redact tokens in error messages and debug logs; no “print config” that includes raw keys

2) Retries
- Retryable: 429, 500/502/503/504, and network/transient transport errors
- Respect Retry-After (seconds or HTTP date)
- Exponential backoff with jitter, capped; default attempts aligned across languages
- Non-retryable: 4xx (except 429) including 400/401/403/404/422

3) Timeouts
- Standard model: overall/request timeout + (where supported) connect/read mapping; consistent naming in constructors
- Streaming: clarify that “overall timeout” applies to request/connection establishment; read timeouts apply to gaps between chunks (language-specific constraints documented)

4) Streaming
- Consistent partial output semantics: callers can access accumulated text before disconnect
- Typed streaming errors include request_id where available
- Documented conservative retry guidance (avoid automatic replay unless idempotency key / safe prompts)

5) Error taxonomy
- Errors include: request_id, status_code (if present), retryable boolean, error_code (where provided by API)

6) Conformance tests
- Shared fixtures for: 429 + Retry-After, 5xx bursts, network flake, timeout, and a streaming interruption path
- CI gate: parity tests required for merges affecting transport/retry/timeout/streaming

## Metrics / results (first 10 days post-stable)
Support + oncall signal (qualitative + early quantitative):
- Fewer “TS works but Python fails under 429” reports; decreased ping-pong between SDK owners
- request_id now present in the majority of SDK-raised errors, speeding up platform log correlation
- No evidence of sustained retry storms after shipping jittered backoff defaults; a few isolated spikes correlated with customer-side custom retry loops

Known caveat: dashboard coverage for streaming disconnect reasons is uneven across languages (Go strongest; Python/TS depend on how users consume events).

## What went well
1) Writing down the standard before implementation
- Having the retry/timeout standard + ADRs prevented each SDK from “doing the obvious thing” differently.

2) Conformance tests caught a real last-minute mismatch
- The 429 handling gap on a streaming path was detected before stable release, not by a customer.

3) Security review early saved churn
- Env var naming + redaction requirements were settled early enough to avoid late rework and risky logging.

4) Platform + SDK coordination improved outcomes
- Gateway changes (Retry-After on 429, request_id propagation, error code enum) made SDK classification reliable.

5) Docs/quickstarts updated in parallel
- Fewer “hidden defaults” surprises because docs now show explicit knobs consistently.

## What didn’t go well / pain points
1) Timeout semantics were still confusing for streaming
- Users interpret “timeout” as “kill the whole stream after X seconds,” but some runtimes treat this as per-read or as only request establishment.
- Our docs got better, but SDK naming still invites confusion (overall vs read).

2) Release coordination overhead
- Shipping three SDKs + gateway changes in a narrow window required more manual tracking than expected.
- Changelog/migration note wording drifted; we had to re-edit after the fact to avoid contradictory guidance.

3) Telemetry/logging fields not consistently exposed
- We aligned fields conceptually (request_id, retry_count, timeout_ms), but some SDKs only expose via debug logs rather than a structured hook.

4) Customer custom retries conflicted with new defaults
- A small number of customers already wrapped SDK calls with their own retry loops; combined with SDK retries this can multiply attempts.
- We need stronger docs guidance: “either use SDK retries or your own, but not both; if both, cap attempts.”

## Remaining parity gaps (as of retro date)
P0/P1 gaps:
- Streaming retry guidance is documented, but SDK behavior for “mid-stream disconnect with partial output” differs subtly:
  - TS: event iteration stops with an error; partial output available if caller accumulates
  - Python: iterator raises typed exception; partial output available via exception field only in newest version
  - Go: returns error with a final state; partial content available through callback buffer pattern
  => Action: define a single recommended pattern in docs + provide helper utilities in each SDK.

- Timeout naming consistency
  - Some SDKs still expose both legacy and new option names; we need to finalize deprecation timeline and remove ambiguity.

P2 gaps:
- Error_code coverage is limited for a few edge endpoints (OpenAI-compat and older routes). This is partially platform-driven.

## Action items (follow-ups)
1) Streaming helper + unified partial output contract (P1)
- Owner: Ibrahim Khan
- Target: 2026-03-20
- Deliverable: small helper in each SDK to accumulate output and return {text, request_id, finish_reason} on success OR throw a typed error containing partial output in a consistent field name.

2) Docs: “Avoid double retries” guidance + examples (P1)
- Owner: Wei Chen
- Target: 2026-03-08
- Deliverable: docs section + snippet per language showing how to disable SDK retries when wrapping with an app-level retry policy.

3) Telemetry hooks API proposal (P2)
- Owner: Logan Wright
- Target: 2026-03-29
- Deliverable: design note for a minimal cross-language hook: onRequestStart/onRetry/onRequestEnd with redacted structured fields.

4) Deprecation plan for legacy timeout/auth option names (P2)
- Owner: Monica Patel + language owners
- Target: 2026-03-15
- Deliverable: explicit timeline (two minor versions), warnings, and migration guide update.

5) Conformance suite: add corporate-proxy streaming fixture (P1)
- Owner: Sahana Iyer + Mateusz Zielinski
- Target: 2026-03-22
- Deliverable: fixture that simulates buffered chunks / half-closed connection; ensure consistent error classification and partial output behavior.

6) Support playbook update: required fields + scripts (P1)
- Owner: Dev Patel
- Target: 2026-03-05
- Deliverable: macro asks for SDK version, request_id, retry_count (if available), timeout config, streaming mode; links to migration notes.

## Process changes (agreed)
1) “Standard first” gate
- Any transport/retry/timeout behavior changes require a standards doc/ADR link in the PR description.

2) Release checklist enforcement
- Use the release checklist as a CI-gated template for SDK release PRs (changelog + migration notes link + conformance tests run ID).

3) Pre-stable customer dogfood list
- Maintain a small group of opt-in customers for beta validation, especially for streaming behind proxies.

## Notes / open questions
- Should we expose idempotency key helpers directly in SDKs (or only document)? Security + product to weigh in.
- Consider aligning default max attempts for streaming to 1 (no auto retry) universally; currently we rely on “don’t retry streaming by default” guidance but behavior differs depending on where failure happens.

## Comms
- Post summary in #devex with a link to this ticket + action items.
- Link this retro from ENG-5120 epic description.
comments: 2026-02-21 (Talia Benson): Scheduled retro for 2026-02-26 10:00 PT. Agenda: metrics, gaps, action items. Please add notes inline before the meeting.

2026-02-26 (Allison Grant): From SRE side: defaults look safe; no thundering herd observed. Biggest remaining risk is customer double-retry. Strongly recommend docs + SDK option to disable retries prominently. Also add an alert for sustained elevated retry_count if we ship telemetry hooks.

2026-02-26 (Marcus Lin): Confirmed we did not regress secret handling. Please ensure any future telemetry hooks are opt-in and explicitly redact auth headers and tokens. Add this as a requirement in the hook proposal.

2026-02-27 (Dana Lo): TS: AbortController plumbing fixed most “timeouts not honored” issues, but some users still expect overall stream duration enforcement. Agree with docs + helper utilities to make partial output handling easier.
2026-02-27 (Sabrina James): Python: partial output in streaming errors is present but discoverability is low. We should standardize field naming and add an example snippet in the streaming guide.
2026-02-28 (Monica Patel): Captured action items above. Marking Done. Creating follow-up tickets for streaming helper + proxy fixture + docs update.
